run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T06:39:59Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on service frontend (otel-demo) is explained by a short, self-limited loss of its two backends. Deployment ad was rolled out (kubectl rollout restart, restartedAt 2026-11-17T06:38:56Z) at 06:38:56Z and Deployment payment at 06:38:55Z; both have a single replica and no readiness/liveness/startup probes, so the replacement pods were marked Ready 2-4 seconds after creation while their containers were still cold-starting. The new ad container (cpu limit 50m) ran at 96.8-99.0% CFS throttling from 06:40Z to 06:47Z and emitted no GetAds spans at all for the minutes 06:41-06:48Z, during which frontend's client spans to AdService/GetAds were 100% ERROR; ad resumed serving at about 06:48Z exactly as its throttling fell to 78/67/28%. The new payment container (cpu limit 20m) was 94% throttled at 06:40-06:41Z, received zero charge spans in the minute ending 06:42Z and recovered by about 06:43Z. That produced frontend ERROR spans on /api/data and /api/checkout (four spans per failed request: GET, GET /api/data, executing api route, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds - 407.68 each - plus 79.3 each on the checkout path and 15.25 tcp.connect), and matching frontend-proxy ingress/egress 5xx spans. Traffic volume was flat, callers were not CPU-starved, and no other service emitted request-path errors. The flagd ConfigMap currently declares adFailure=on and paymentUnreachable=on; that is reported as an unresolved alternative hypothesis, because the two services recovered at different times matching their own throttling and the flags are still on while errors have returned to zero. Facts about the pod restart trigger, span-level error text and the alert rule itself remain gaps.

claims.text: Frontend error spans were absent before the incident and began in the minute ending 06:40:00Z (86 spans), peaked at 728 in the minute ending 06:42:00Z, stayed 316-504 through the minute ending 06:47:00Z, fell to 192 in the minute ending 06:48:00Z and were 0 in the minute ending 06:50:00Z (1-minute increases of frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans).

In the hour ending 06:58:46Z the frontend's ERROR-status spans were: grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 407.68, GET /api/data 407.68, GET 407.68, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' 407.68, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 79.3, POST /api/checkout 79.3, POST 79.3, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 79.3 and tcp.connect 15.25 (about 1963 error spans in total, roughly 83% of them on the ad path).

The ad service emitted zero oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans in each of the minutes ending 06:42-06:48Z, while frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans in those minutes were 126, 78, 120, 112, 96, 126 and 48 ERROR with 0 UNSET; ad inbound GetAds spans returned to 40 in the minute ending 06:48:00Z and 100 in the minute ending 06:50:00Z.

Deployment ad was rolled out at 06:38:56Z: ReplicaSet ad-5f8dd7c58d was created with annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:38:56Z and an otherwise identical pod template (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, same env and resources) to the previous ReplicaSet ad-554b849958; events show Deployment ad 'Scaled up replica set ad-5f8dd7c58d from 0 to 1' at 06:38:56Z, pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started at 06:38:56-58Z, and 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0' with pod ad-554b849958-6z62j Killing at 06:38:58Z.

The replacement ad pod was marked Ready at 06:38:58Z, two seconds after creation (container ad startedAt 06:38:58Z, restartCount 0), and Deployment ad declares no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe on container ad (rollingUpdate maxSurge 25%, maxUnavailable 25%).
Deployment ad sets container limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi and Deployment payment sets cpu 20m / memory 160Mi, both with replicas: 1 and images from ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3 (ad, payment).

The new ad pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 consumed 0.095-0.098 cores with 96.8-99.0% CFS throttling in the minutes ending 06:40-06:47Z, then throttling dropped to 78.4% (06:48), 66.8% (06:49) and 28.3% (06:50) and usage to 0.033/0.042/0.018 cores; the previous ad pod ad-554b849958-6z62j had run at only 0.008-0.024 cores with 4-33% throttling between 06:18Z and 06:39Z.

The replacement ad pod's memory working set climbed from 4.98 MB at 06:39:00Z to 692 MB at 06:50:00Z (the previous ad pod had been steady around 666-694 MB), and the ad container's retained log lines in 06:38-06:56Z start only at 06:48:06Z.

Deployment payment was rolled out at 06:38:55Z (ReplicaSet payment-5d565cf9b created with kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:38:55Z, identical template, image 2.1.3-payment; old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 scaled to 0 and pod payment-55766d76b9-9fxhp killed at 06:38:59Z); the replacement pod payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn was Ready at 06:38:59Z, was 94.5%/94.0% throttled in the minutes ending 06:40/06:41Z (falling to 13-36% by 06:44-06:47Z), and payment emitted 0 charge spans in the minute ending 06:42:00Z while checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and PlaceOrder error spans were 12 in the minute ending 06:40:00Z and 56 in the minute ending 06:42:00Z, then 0.

frontend-proxy recorded ERROR spans on its own 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' operations during exactly the same minutes (32 and 28 at 06:40, peaks 176 and 174 at 06:42, 78/78 at 06:43, 126/124 at 06:44, 122/124 at 06:48, 2/0 at 06:50), while total ingress spans stayed flat at about 1146-1496 per minute from 06:35Z to 06:50Z.

The calling services were not resource-starved during the burst: the frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-68tcg stayed at 22-36% CFS throttling and the checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-vxwlj at 0% throughout the minutes 06:35-06:49Z.

Neither ad nor payment produced ERROR-status spans of their own in the hour: their only ERROR series are flagd calls (ad flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean 1.33 and EventStream 1.02 per hour, fraud-detection EventStream 1.02, recommendation /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 4.07); the failing GetAds and Charge spans exist only as client spans recorded on frontend and checkout.

The other downstream services showed no error spans in the hour and kept serving normal traffic: currency (Currency/Convert 3451.58 calls, 0 error), cart (HGET 10231.73, POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 6604.27, 0 error), product-catalog (GetProduct 21176.15, 0 error), shipping, email, quote, accounting and image-provider likewise had no ERROR-status series.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo (key demo.flagd.json) currently declares flag adFailure defaultVariant "on" ("Fail ad service") and flag paymentUnreachable defaultVariant "on" ("Payment service is unavailable"), with every other flag (adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) defaultVariant "off".

Separately from this cause, the fraud-detection container was OOMKilled (last termination reason OOMKilled, exit code 137, finishedAt 06:40:42Z, restartCount 1, now Ready); its own error spans in the hour were 1.02 on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream.

Primary explanation: the 06:38:56Z rollout of Deployment ad replaced its only replica with a container that was immediately treated as Ready (no readiness probe) while its JVM cold-started under a 50m CPU limit; sustained 97-99% CFS throttling kept it from accepting/serving gRPC calls until about 06:48Z, which is why every frontend AdService/GetAds call failed and /api/data returned errors during that period; the same pattern on Deployment payment at 06:38:55Z (20m CPU limit, 94% throttled) explains the shorter checkout->payment failures at 06:40-06:42Z.

Unresolved alternative: the flagd fault-injection flags adFailure="on" and paymentUnreachable="on" in ConfigMap flagd-config were active in the window and made ad and payment fail their callers. It is kept only as a hypothesis: the ConfigMap state was read at 06:59Z (after the window), there is no change history showing when the values were written or what flagd served during the window, and no ad/payment server-side ERROR spans exist.

What makes the flagd-flag explanation inconsistent with the observations: both flags are still "on" in the ConfigMap while frontend error spans returned to 0 in the minute ending 06:50:00Z and ad served 100 GetAds spans then; and the two affected services recovered at different times (payment by about 06:43Z, ad by about 06:48Z) that track each pod's own throttling curve rather than a common flag switch, while ad and payment produced no ERROR spans themselves (their callers' calls never reached them).

Misconfigured ad/payment networking is not supported by the objects read: Service ad (ClusterIP 100.70.166.37, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad) and Service payment (ClusterIP 100.64.198.79, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment) both currently have endpoints pointing at the running replacement pods ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 (100.96.1.149) and payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn (100.96.1.157).

Rejected: a traffic surge or load-generator flood caused the frontend error rate. frontend-proxy ingress volume was flat at about 1146-1496 spans/min before, during and after the burst while error spans rose from 0 to 176/min and back to 2/min.

Rejected: frontend or checkout being CPU-starved caused their own outbound calls to fail; frontend pod throttling stayed at 22-36% and checkout at 0% across the burst, and their non-ad/non-payment calls (cart, product-catalog, currency, recommendation) continued without ERROR spans.

Fix the availability gap on Deployment ad (and Deployment payment): add readiness and startup probes so a cold container is not put in the Service endpoints, raise the container CPU limits (ad 50m, payment 20m) so JVM/Node startup is not throttled at about 99%, and consider 2 replicas and maxUnavailable 0 so a rollout does not remove the only serving pod.

Confirm with whoever operates this cluster what issued the rollout restarts of Deployment ad and Deployment payment at 06:38:55-56Z, and review whether the flagd config values adFailure="on" and paymentUnreachable="on" are intended, since those flags inject exactly the failure modes seen if they are ever honoured.

Investigate the fraud-detection OOMKilled restart (exit 137 at 06:40:42Z) against its 400Mi memory limit; it is not evidence for the frontend alert but is an independent container failure in the same window.

gaps: No change-history integration is available, so who or what triggered the kubectl rollout restarts of Deployment ad (restartedAt 2026-11-17T06:38:56Z) and Deployment payment (restartedAt 2026-11-17T06:38:55Z) cannot be established from the evidence.

Jaeger returned no traces for service frontend in 06:38-06:48Z or 06:50-06:58:46Z (queries returned nothing); the newest traces it returned were from 06:23:31Z, so the exact gRPC status code and error message of the failed GetAds/Charge calls could not be read.
The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 06:38-06:56Z (0 bytes read), so its own error text could not be checked.
list_prometheus_rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate returned nothing (no_data), so the alert's exact expression, lookback and reported value (4.4222) are unverified.
Trace-derived metrics end at about 06:50Z, so the frontend error rate after 06:50Z is unknown.
A query for NetworkPolicy objects in otel-demo returned no objects (status no_data), so the absence of a network policy blocking ad/payment cannot be treated as proven.
The flagd ConfigMap was read at 06:59Z, after the window; the values flagd actually served during 06:39-06:49Z and the time any ConfigMap edit was made are unknown (no change history).
The cause of the fraud-detection OOMKill (exit 137 at 06:40:42Z) is not established, and no evidence ties it to the frontend error burst.

The payment container's own logs sample only from 06:47:52Z onward and the ad container's retained log lines only from 06:48:06Z, so their behaviour during the outage minutes is not directly logged in what could be read.
next_steps: Ask the cluster operator or change system to identify the change that restarted Deployment ad and Deployment payment at 06:38:55-56Z.
Ship a readiness probe and startup probe on the ad and payment containers and raise their CPU limits; then verify a rollout no longer removes serving capacity.
Review and, if unintended, reset the flagd flags adFailure and paymentUnreachable in ConfigMap flagd-config.
Review fraud-detection's 400Mi memory limit and its recent OOMKilled restart.
